Aura of Courage.description: Starting at 3rd level, a paladin becomes completely immune to fear, whether magical or mundane. Every ally within 10 feet of her receives a +4 morale bonus on saving throws against fear effects. This aura operates only while the paladin remains conscious; it ceases to function if she falls unconscious or dies.

Aura of Good.description: The intensity of a paladin's good aura (as perceived by appropriate detection effects) equals her paladin level, equivalent to that of a cleric who serves a good-aligned deity.

Detect Evil.description: A paladin can use detect evil at will, functioning identically to the spell of the same name.

Divine Grace.description: Upon reaching 2nd level, a paladin adds her Charisma bonus (if any) to all saving throws.

Divine Health.description: At 3rd level, a paladin becomes immune to all forms of disease, including those of supernatural and magical origin (such as mummy rot and lycanthropy).

Lay on Hands.description: From 2nd level onward, a paladin with a Charisma score of 12 or higher can mend injuries through physical contact, whether her own or those of others. Her daily healing pool equals her paladin level multiplied by her Charisma bonus. For instance, a 7th-level paladin with 16 Charisma (+3 bonus) can restore up to 21 hit points per day. This healing can be split among multiple individuals and need not be used all at once. Activating this ability requires a standard action. Alternatively, the paladin may direct some or all of this healing energy to harm undead creatures instead. Doing so requires a successful melee touch attack and does not provoke an attack of opportunity. The paladin chooses how many points from her daily pool to expend as damage after landing the touch against the undead target.

Remove Disease.description: Beginning at 6th level, a paladin can produce a remove disease effect identical to the spell once per week. For every three paladin levels gained beyond 6th, she can use this ability one additional time per week (twice at 9th, three times at 12th, and so on).

Smite Evil.description: Once per day, a paladin can channel righteous fury into a single normal melee strike against an evil target. She applies her Charisma bonus (if any) to the attack roll and inflicts 1 additional point of damage per paladin level. For instance, a 13th-level paladin wielding a longsword would deal 1d8+13 damage, plus any other applicable bonuses from high Strength or magical effects. If the target turns out not to be evil, the smite produces no effect but still expends one daily use. At 5th level and every five levels after that, the paladin gains one more daily use of this ability, reaching a maximum of five uses per day at 20th level.

Special Mount.description: At 5th level, a paladin receives the service of a remarkably intelligent, powerful, and faithful steed to accompany her on her righteous mission. This mount is typically a heavy warhorse (for Medium paladins) or a warpony (for Small paladins). Once per day as a full-round action, the paladin may magically summon her mount from the celestial planes where it dwells. The mount materializes adjacent to the paladin and stays for 2 hours per paladin level; it can be sent back at any time as a free action. The same creature answers each summons, though the paladin may choose to release a particular mount from service (for example, if it has become too aged). Whenever summoned, the mount arrives at full health regardless of prior injuries, and it appears with any gear it was wearing or carrying when last dismissed (including barding, saddle, saddlebags, and similar equipment). Summoning the mount is a conjuration (calling) effect with an effective spell level equal to one-third the paladin's level. If the mount perishes, it vanishes immediately, leaving behind any carried equipment. The paladin cannot summon a replacement for thirty days or until she gains another paladin level, whichever occurs first - even if the mount is somehow resurrected. Throughout this thirty-day waiting period, the paladin suffers a -1 penalty on attack rolls and weapon damage rolls.

Spells.description: Starting at 4th level, a paladin acquires the ability to cast a limited selection of divine spells drawn from the paladin spell list. Spells must be chosen and prepared ahead of time. To prepare or cast a given spell, the paladin needs a Wisdom score of at least 10 + the spell's level (Wisdom 11 for 1st-level spells, Wisdom 12 for 2nd-level spells, and so on). The saving throw DC against a paladin's spell equals 10 + the spell's level + the paladin's Wisdom modifier. Like other casters, a paladin is limited to a certain number of spells per level each day, as shown in the class table. A high Wisdom score grants additional bonus spells per day. When the class table indicates 0 spells of a given level, the paladin receives only whatever bonus spells her Wisdom score provides for that level. Paladins have no access to domain spells or domain-granted powers. A paladin prepares and casts spells in the manner of a cleric but cannot sacrifice a prepared spell to spontaneously cast a cure spell. Any spell on the paladin spell list may be prepared and cast, so long as the paladin can cast that spell level, though she must select her spells during daily meditation. Through 3rd level, a paladin possesses no caster level. From 4th level onward, her caster level equals half her paladin level.

Turn Undead.description: At 4th level, a paladin gains the supernatural capacity to turn undead. The number of daily uses equals 3 + her Charisma modifier. Her effective turning ability is equivalent to a cleric three levels lower than her paladin level.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: Paladins have proficiency with every simple and martial weapon, all armor types (light, medium, and heavy), and all shields other than tower shields.

overrides.description: Driven by righteousness, bound by a strict moral code, and empowered to vanquish wickedness - these define the paladin's calling. Only a rare few possess the unwavering virtue needed to follow this path, but those who do gain the ability to shield the innocent, mend the wounded, and strike down the corrupt. In a world teeming with scheming spellcasters, profane clergy, savage dragons, and demonic horrors, the paladin stands as an unyielding beacon of hope. Paladins approach every adventure with earnest purpose, often treating even simple tasks as sacred quests. Each mission represents a chance to prove their valor, sharpen their combat prowess, refine their strategy, and seek opportunities for benevolence. Yet a paladin truly shines when spearheading a grand crusade against the forces of darkness, rather than simply plundering forgotten ruins. Holy power shields the paladin and grants extraordinary capabilities. It deflects harm, renders the paladin resistant to disease, enables self-healing, and fortifies the spirit against terror. The paladin can extend this power to aid companions, restoring their vitality or purging their ailments. Ultimately, this divine energy can be channeled to annihilate evil. Even a novice paladin can sense the presence of evil, while veterans can deliver devastating blows against wicked foes and repel undead. Furthermore, this sacred bond attracts a powerful steed to the paladin's side, imbuing the mount with enhanced strength, intellect, and mystical resilience.
